title: No Evidence, No Excuse: Vietnam Needs Transparent Dog-Trade Reform
excerpt: Verified reporting must separate rabies exposure, pet theft, and commercial trade. Vietnam needs transparent enforcement and a clear abolition pathway.
body_html:
Families deserve facts before slogans. Current material does not identify a verified seizure, court judgment, poisoning incident, or named Vietnamese agency that can support stronger claims about this trade. That gap does not protect operators. It demands transparent evidence, public enforcement records, and protection for Vietnamese families and their companion animals.

Separate risks. Demand proof.

Rabies exposure occurs when infected saliva enters broken skin or mucous membranes through bites or scratches. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical care for post-exposure prophylaxis, including vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. See World Health Organization guidance.

Household rabies incidents and commercial dog transport represent separate biosecurity questions. Neither proves the other caused it. Pet theft, illegal transport, quarantine evasion, slaughter, and food safety failures require incident-level evidence: dates, locations, agencies, seizures, prosecutions, and laboratory findings.

Vietnamese leadership can close the gap

Lawful activity, regulatory breaches, and criminal theft need clear distinctions. Vietnamese communities already protect families, pets, and public health through local reporting and reform demands. SDE calls for nationwide abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition and add your name to a public demand that reaches decision-makers.

Evidence must lead reform—not myths about Vietnam’s dog trade.

• Current material identifies no verifiable Vietnamese seizure, court judgment, poisoning case, named agency, or laboratory finding supporting broader claims.
• Rabies spreads through infected saliva entering bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes—not through properly cooked meat as an established route.
• After possible exposure: wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical care for post-exposure prophylaxis before symptoms develop.
• Household rabies incidents and commercial transport risks must remain separate unless primary evidence proves a link.
• Transparent records can expose theft, illegal transport, quarantine breaches, and unsafe slaughter.

No scene, victim, or criminal network should be invented to create outrage.

Rabies exposure occurs when infected saliva enters broken skin or mucous membranes through bites or scratches. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Household exposure and commercial dog transport remain separate questions unless primary evidence connects them. Vietnamese community leaders, families, veterinarians, and officials can demand records, enforce quarantine, investigate theft, and close legal gaps.
